name: PT Alkindo Naratama Tbk

frontmatter.title: Alkindo Naratama: a converter priced for a recovery it may not repeat
frontmatter.summary: SELL, target Rp386, a total return of -72.7%. The model now starts from the 9M2026 actual: revenue IDR1,882.7bn, gross profit IDR412.4bn and net profit IDR172.7bn [S5], with depreciation restated from the annual report notes [S4]. The base gross margin is 21.9%, the interim level, fading to 17.0% by FY2030E. Even so the shares carry 110.2x trailing and 21.1x forward earnings.
thesis: The step-up is real: nine-month 2026 net profit of IDR172.7bn on revenue of IDR1,882.7bn, against IDR35.3bn for the whole of FY2025 [S5][S0].
The cost line is imported: recovered paper is bought abroad in dollars, so the 9M2026 gross margin of 21.9% is an input-cost and currency swing, not a structural shift [S4].
Volume is capped: the converting plant used 38.5 of 40.5 of capacity in FY2025 [S4], so growth is price and mix, and the base fades to 4.5%.
The cash cycle is heavy: working capital of 25.0% of revenue makes free cash flow lag profit, though the base still deleverages, net debt to EBITDA falling from 3.2 to 0.1 [S0].
Control and float: the controller holds just over two-thirds of 2,700,713,744 shares and one local individual a further quarter [S4], so a 20.0% liquidity discount sits on the target.

catalysts.event: FY2026 financial statements; gross margin outcome against the base case
End of the authorised share buyback window

blocks.text: **Rating SELL; target Rp386, a total return of -72.7%.** Our fundamental value is Rp427 per share, rolled to Rp470 for the twelve months and weighted across scenarios to Rp482, and the liquidity discount of 20.0% on a float this thin takes the target we publish to Rp386. Against a market price of Rp1,445: this revision rebuilt the base case on the 9M2026 interim [S5] and restated depreciation from the annual report [S4]; the value is materially higher than at initiation, but the price has moved further. At 110.2x trailing earnings and 21.1x our FY2026E earnings, the market is not just capitalising the recovery shown in the interim — it is capitalising that recovery as permanent, at a margin above the 9M2026 record.

That multiple, and the size of the expected return, are measured against a quote that is not a considered market view. The pack's high‑to‑low span over the trailing year is Rp525 to Rp1,955 and average daily traded value is only IDR385.1m [S0]; IDX put ALDO under unusual‑market‑activity watch on 15 October 2026, suspended trading on 16 October and lifted the suspension on 19 October, and the stock then fell -29.9% in the week to 23 October [S8][S9][S10]. We do not change the fundamental value for this — the asset is worth what its cash flows are worth — but the reader should treat the expected return as the distance from a thin, post‑UMA speculative print to fair value, not as a forecast that the price falls by that amount within twelve months.

Three things drive the SELL. First, the margin step-up is an input-cost and currency swing: the interim gross margin of 21.9% is the highest in the four-year record in the annual report [S4], and it is set by dollar-priced recovered paper, which the FY2025 management discussion names as the margin channel [S4]. Second, the cash cycle is heavy: working capital of 25.0% of revenue means profit of IDR184.3bn does not become cash on the same timeline, and free cash flow to the firm of IDR156.4bn sits well below the earnings line [S0]. Third, the float is thin: the controller holds just over two-thirds and one local individual a further quarter of 2,700,713,744 shares [S4], so a value claim has to survive a 20.0% discount on a tape where entry and exit move the price — a tape the exchange itself flagged for counter-directional movement and then suspended in October 2026 [S8][S9].

**What moves the value.** The target is most sensitive to gross margin, then to the discount rate. On the grid in section four each point of gross margin is worth more than each point of terminal growth, and the most optimistic corner of the twelve-month grid — two points of margin and four points of growth above base — is still less than half the traded price. The cross-checks in section four are a range, not a single point: the EV/EBITDA method returns Rp465 per share on a trailing basis and roughly the traded price on the model's own forward EBITDA, the P/E method returns Rp111 on the trough year, and the discounted cash flow returns Rp462. The DCF is the method that prices the forecast, so it is the anchor; the spread between the three is the honest measure of how much of this valuation rests on which year one capitalises.

Paper converting sits in the middle of the packaging chain: base paper made from recovered fibre is cut, coated, laminated and formed into tubes, cores, edge protectors and boxes for industrial customers. It is a service-heavy business in principle, but it becomes capital-intensive when a converter owns the paper machine that feeds it, as Alkindo does through its subsidiary. Pricing power is limited because the product is specified by the customer and the alternative suppliers are numerous.

PT Alkindo Naratama Tbk makes packaging out of paper. It runs two lines — a paper line and a chemicals line — and describes itself as an integrated paper and chemicals group headquartered in West Bandung, West Java [S4]. The paper line is the larger and the more cyclical of the two. It converts base paper into tubes, cores, honeycomb board, edge protectors, boxes, bags, hexa wrap and related protective packaging, sold almost entirely business to business to industrial customers [S4]. The chemicals line, run through two subsidiaries, distributes textile dyestuffs and auxiliaries and manufactures water-based polymers used in adhesives and coatings [S4].

The structure matters for the economics. The converting business itself is a fabrication and service operation: the company cuts, coats, laminates and forms paper to customer specification, and its stated competitive advantage is flexibility — thickness, dimension, colour and finishing options — rather than proprietary product [S4]. Behind it sits PT Eco Paper Indonesia, the subsidiary that owns the brown-paper capability and produces core board, kraftliner, greyboard and duplex board, the substrates the converters consume [S4]. That is partial vertical integration, but it stops short of fibre: the brown-paper machine runs on recovered paper, chiefly old corrugated cardboard, much of it imported [S4]. The group therefore buys its single largest input in world markets, in dollars, and sells converted packaging into a competitive domestic market.

Capacity and utilisation tell the same story of a mature asset base. Installed converting capacity at the end of FY2025 was 40.5 a year, and the company reports utilisation of 38.5 over the year [S4]. Paper-segment volume was 234.9 thousand tonnes against 39.1 thousand tonnes in the converting segment [S4]. In other words, the converting plant is running close to its stated capacity, so incremental volume must come either from the paper machine, from debottlenecking, or from price and mix rather than from spare capacity.

**Strategy and footprint.** Management's stated priorities for FY2025 were continuous innovation in sustainable packaging, customer‑specific customisation, quality certification and cost efficiency, with a deliberate extension from pure business‑to‑business selling into small and medium enterprises through products such as paper boxes, bags, cups, bowls and buckets [S4]. The company also reports having entered export markets in several countries while remaining predominantly domestic [S4]. It holds ISO quality‑management certification and Forest Stewardship Council chain‑of‑custody certification for its recycled‑fibre products, which it uses as a marketing differentiator with international buyers facing packaging‑sustainability rules [S4].

**Revenue mix.** Consolidated revenue in FY2025 was IDR2,119.2bn, of which paper was the majority and chemicals the smaller share; the annual report records the paper segment growing sales by a double-digit percentage and chemicals by a mid-single-digit percentage over the prior year [S4]. Both lines are exposed to imported input costs — recovered paper in the paper line, petrochemical intermediates in the chemicals line — so the group's gross margin moves with the rupiah and with global commodity prices rather than with domestic demand alone.

**Ownership and control.** The controlling shareholder is PT Golden Arista International, which held just over two-thirds of the 2,700,713,744 issued shares at the end of FY2025 and is identified in the annual report as the major and controlling shareholder; its beneficial owners are two named family members [S4]. One local individual — listed in the ownership table as a public holder, not as an affiliate or controller — held a further quarter [S4], and the board of commissioners and directors hold small individual stakes in aggregate [S4]. The company holds 4,554,100 treasury shares from its buyback [S4]. That leaves only about a seventh of the issued shares in unaffiliated public hands, below the data pack's free float of 13.7%, which presumably counts part of that individual's block [S0]. The investable float is genuinely small, which is a structural feature of the name, not a temporary condition, and it is why a liquidity discount of 20.0% sits on the final target.

Converted-paper packaging is a fragmented industry almost everywhere. The technology is widely available, customers specify the product, and switching costs are low once a specification is qualified. Scale advantages come from procurement of base paper and from logistics density around industrial clusters rather than from brand. That is why converters usually earn mid-single-digit operating margins through the cycle and why the paper machine, when a converter owns one, is both the source of cost advantage and the source of capital intensity.

The Indonesian pulp and paper industry is large, export-oriented and politically visible. The annual report puts its contribution to non-oil-and-gas processing GDP at just under four per cent, with more than a quarter of a million direct employees and a further million-plus indirect jobs across the operating companies in the sector [S4]. It is a net exporter: pulp exports run at several billion dollars a year and paper exports at a similar order of magnitude, and the country ranks among the ten largest producers in the world in both pulp and paper, and among the top few in Asia [S4]. That national picture, however, describes the integrated producers with pulp mills and forest concessions. Alkindo does not operate at that scale; it sits several steps downstream, in converting and in recycled brown paper.

**Where Alkindo sits.** The converting segment is fragmented. Barriers to entry in simple conversion are low, customers are industrial and price-sensitive, and the product is specified rather than branded. The annual report's own account of competition emphasises flexibility and customisation — thickness, dimension, colour, coating — rather than cost leadership or proprietary technology [S4]. That is a real but narrow moat: it supports customer retention at the margin, not pricing power through a cost shock.

**The cost driver.** The dominant swing factor is the price of recovered paper, known in the trade as old corrugated cardboard, which the company buys largely from abroad and pays for in dollars [S4]. The FY2025 management discussion is explicit that rupiah depreciation raised the cost of imported raw material and compressed margin, and that this was the main reason profitability lagged despite higher sales [S4]. The second driver is energy, which the company also flags as a cost pressure in the same discussion [S4]. The third is domestic industrial production, which sets packaging demand; the annual report notes manufacturing growth and a purchasing managers' index in expansion through the year [S4]. None of these three is under the company's control, and two of the three are priced in dollars.

**Macro transmission.** Our house macro deck has the rupiah at Rp18,350/USD against the dollar in FY2027E, versus a spot of Rp17,633/USD, with a long-run assumption of Rp19,000/USD. A depreciating path is a persistent cost headwind for a converter that buys recovered paper offshore and sells domestically, and it is the single most important external variable in our forecast. The macro regime we are working under — balance-of-payments pressure — biases the risk to the weaker side of that channel [S4].

**Regulation and policy.** The binding regulation for this industry is environmental rather than tariff-based: sustainability certification, chain-of-custody requirements for fibre, and export-market rules on packaging recyclability. Alkindo's Forest Stewardship Council certification and its ISO quality certification are the relevant compliance assets, and the annual report presents them as commercial advantages with international customers [S4]. There is no meaningful tariff protection for domestic converters, which means import competition in finished packaging is a live constraint on price.

**Five forces.** Rivalry is intense: many converters, similar equipment, competition on price and lead time. Supplier power is high in recovered paper, where global collection and Chinese demand set the price, and moderate in chemicals, where the company is a distributor for international brands. Buyer power is moderate to high: industrial customers qualify a supplier and then shop the specification, so volume is won on service and lost on price. The threat of new entrants is moderate in simple converting and low in brown paper, where the machine is the barrier. Substitutes are the interesting long-run force: plastic and flexible packaging compete on cost and performance, while sustainability regulation pushes demand the other way, toward fibre. On balance this is a structurally low-margin industry with cyclical margins, and the correct valuation posture is a through-cycle margin, not a peak one [S4].

**Market position.** The company does not disclose market share, and we would not rely on one if it did, because the relevant market — converted protective packaging for West Java industry — is not measured by any published series. What can be said is that Alkindo is a mid-sized specialist with a regional manufacturing base, a partial raw-material integration through its paper subsidiary, and a customer base that values customisation [S4]. It is a challenger, not a leader, and it competes against both small converters and the packaging arms of integrated paper groups.

**The history.** Revenue rose from IDR1,401.9bn in FY2022 to IDR2,119.2bn in FY2025, a steady mid-teens compounding that reflects volume and, in the latest year, a double-digit increase in paper-segment sales [S4]. Profit did not follow. Gross margin compressed from 18.2% in FY2022 to 14.8% in FY2025, operating profit moved from IDR103.8bn to IDR92.4bn, and net profit from IDR65.3bn to IDR35.3bn, with a loss of IDR-8.9bn in FY2024 [S0]. The shape is a classic commodity squeeze: volume up, revenue up, margin down, and interest expense rising in the background from IDR15.5bn to IDR46.4bn as debt was added [S0]. The FY2025 management discussion attributes the cost pressure to higher recovered-paper prices and rupiah depreciation, and to energy costs [S4].

**The interim is the new base.** The 9M2026 report is the pivot of this revision [S5]. Nine-month revenue of IDR1,882.7bn was a fifth ahead of IDR1,556.3bn in the same period a year earlier; gross profit of IDR412.4bn against IDR225.6bn, which puts the interim margin at 21.9%, above every annual level in the FY2022-to-FY2025 record [S0]; and net profit of IDR172.7bn, with basic earnings per share of 63.95 for the period against 7.87 a year earlier [S5]. We read that as lower recovered-paper costs and a steadier rupiah running through the imported cost line, not as a change in the business model [S4]. The base case therefore starts at the interim actual and does not haircut it. FY2026E revenue of IDR2,500.7bn grows 18.0% on the last actual; against the nine‑month actual of IDR1,882.7bn this implies a fourth quarter a little above the prior‑year seasonal quarter, not the full‑year extrapolation of the 9M2026 run‑rate. FY2026E net profit of IDR184.3bn is built from the full‑year margin and cost base; against the nine‑month actual of IDR172.7bn it leaves only a small fourth‑quarter increment, because a full year of interest is charged and because the model applies the full‑year effective tax rate of 26.2% to the whole year while the nine‑month accounts paid a lower effective rate on a smaller pre‑tax base — the difference is a fourth‑quarter tax true‑up, not a collapse in the fourth‑quarter margin [S5][S0].

**The forecast.** Revenue growth fades from 18.0% in FY2026E to 5.0% by FY2030E: the converting plant already used 38.5 of 40.5 of stated capacity in FY2025 [S4], so the early-year growth is price, mix and recovered-paper pass-through rather than physical debottlenecking, and no expansion project is disclosed that would justify a step-up in capex [S4]. Gross margin starts at the interim actual of 21.9% and fades to 17.0% by FY2030E: the interim is above the FY2022 peak of 18.2%, the business names no moat beyond customisation, and the dollar-priced input is cyclical, so we do not capitalise a record margin for a decade [S4][S5]. Operating expenses hold at 10.0% of revenue, the 9M2026 level [S5]. Depreciation is restated at 3.4% of revenue — the FY2025 charge of IDR70.8bn over revenue — against the small figure the data pack carried, and that restatement is the single largest change in this revision [S4]. Sustaining capex is 3.0% of revenue, just below the restated depreciation, with no announced expansion; reported capex ran below depreciation in both FY2024 and FY2025 [S4], so we hold a maintenance‑only regime deliberately and say plainly that if the machine must be replaced at the depreciation rate the value falls [S4]. Working capital is 25.0% of revenue, between the FY2025 actual and the three-year average [S0]. The effective tax rate is the rate the FY2025 accounts show being paid [S0].

**Cash flow and the balance sheet.** The forecast turns cash positive from the first year: free cash flow to the firm of IDR156.4bn in FY2026E, rising to IDR167.0bn by FY2035E, against negative cash flow in FY2025 [S0]. The drag is the working-capital cycle — the FY2025 increase of IDR151.7bn was more than the operating profit of the year, and the forecast carries 25.0% of revenue into the future [S0]. Net debt of IDR529.9bn at the FY2025 year-end falls to IDR42.4bn by FY2030E on positive cash flow with no new borrowing, and the model reaches net cash around FY2031E [S0]; net debt to EBITDA moves from 3.2 to 0.1 on restated EBITDA [S4]. For history the FY2025 year-end position was gross debt of IDR612.2bn against cash of IDR82.3bn [S0], and the annual report records bank debt to equity at a little over half of equity [S4]; the valuation bridge, by contrast, is struck on the newer balance sheet, the 9M2026 interim [S5], because today's enterprise value has to net the debt that exists today, not the debt at the last year-end. Interest cover is the number to watch: IDR46.4bn of interest against IDR92.4bn of operating profit in FY2025 is about two times, widening to about six times on FY2026E operating profit [S0].

**Capital allocation.** The company pays a small, steady dividend — 0.50 per share in FY2025, a payout of 3.8% of earnings, and the forecast holds 12.0% [S0]. In June 2026 the shareholders approved a buyback of up to Rp10.0 billion, to run for a year [S6]. At this price the buyback is small relative to market capitalisation, and we would rather see the cash applied to debt; but with the forecast deleveraging, it no longer competes with a funding need as it did in the initiation build [S0].

**Earnings quality.** Three flags survive this revision, and one was the point of it. First, the data pack understates depreciation: the notes charge IDR70.8bn in FY2025 and IDR68.5bn in FY2024, including IDR4.8bn inside selling expenses alone, against the pack figure; the model now restates D&A from the notes and every EBITDA-based conclusion here uses the restated line [S4]. Second, the accruals habit is real: the FY2025 working-capital increase of IDR151.7bn consumed more than the operating profit, so earnings outran cash even in a good year, and the forecast carries the same intensity [S0]. Third, the free float is thin and the controller holds just over two-thirds: price discovery is weak and minority holders have little influence [S4]. The exchange flagged the stock for unusual market activity on 15 October 2026 and suspended it between 16 October and 19 October 2026, before it fell -29.9% in the following week [S8][S9][S10]. We found no notation letters, pledged controller shares or related-party sales above the disclosed threshold; the audit opinion is unqualified, from the same firm for the prior years [S4].

**Why this method set.** Alkindo is a cyclical converter with a dollar-priced input, a heavy working-capital cycle and a thin float. That argues for a discounted cash flow as the primary method, with earnings and EBITDA multiples as cross-checks rather than as the anchor, because a multiple applied to a trough or a peak year is a disguised forecast. We therefore weight the discounted cash flow at 70.0%, the EV/EBITDA method at 20.0% and the earnings method at 10.0%. The earnings weight is deliberately small: the peer median is struck on trailing peer earnings, and a forward peer multiple would require forward peer estimates, which this house does not use, so the multiple methods here are trailing by construction and FY2025 is the trough year. The blend is Rp427 per share, Rp470 after the twelve-month roll and Rp482 after the scenario weighting; the liquidity discount of 20.0% takes the final target to Rp386, because the float is thin enough that the quoted price is a poor estimate of realisable value.

**The cash flow result.** The discounted cash flow returns Rp462 per share on an enterprise value of IDR1,789.1bn, with the terminal value carrying 50.8% of the total and positive at both ends: every explicit-period free cash flow is positive, from IDR156.4bn in FY2026E to IDR167.0bn in FY2035E [S0]. This is not a floor artefact and it is not a nil result — the earlier negative terminal value came from a forecast built before the interim and before the depreciation restatement, and it has been eliminated by rebuilding the base case, not by capping it. What the value expresses is a through-cycle margin business earning a discount rate of 11.2% with terminal growth of 4.0%.

**Why the DCF sits so far below the price.** The DCF's enterprise value of IDR1,789.1bn is a low multiple of FY2026E EBITDA of IDR381.4bn, and that is the whole argument with the market's valuation: the DCF charges the working-capital build of IDR72.0bn a year and maintenance capex of IDR75.0bn, and it carries depreciation at 3.4% of revenue, while an EBITDA multiple charges for none of those. Free cash flow to the firm of IDR156.4bn is less than half FY2026E EBITDA, because the working-capital build, maintenance capex and cash tax together take more of it than the depreciation line adds back, so a buyer paying an EBITDA multiple is paying for earnings before the charges that consume the majority of the cash [S0]. We regard the multiple the traded price implies — 11.3x our FY2026E EBITDA — as requiring that this business be sold at exit on the same multiple, on a margin we do not expect to be the through-cycle level; that is multiple expansion, and we do not pay for it.

**Cost of capital.** The blended after-tax cost of capital is 11.2%, inside the house band for rupiah assets. The cost of equity of 11.9% is built from a risk-free rate of 7.4%, an equity risk premium for mature markets of 4.2%, a country risk premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 0.90 from an unlevered beta of 0.80 at a debt-to-equity ratio of 16.4%. The pre‑tax cost of debt of 9.4% is the house deck's risk‑free rate of 7.4% plus a corporate spread. That is a forward rate, above the realised history: the model's own cost‑of‑debt input is 8.0%, the three‑year average of interest expense over opening total debt, and FY2025 interest expense of IDR46.4bn on opening debt of IDR581.0bn is consistent with it [S0]. The gap between the two is the refinancing assumption, not an inconsistency. Weights are 85.9% equity and 14.1% debt, on market values. We have not added a size or governance premium on top of the country risk premium; the thin float is instead handled through the liquidity discount applied to the final target.

**Cross-checks: what each year is worth.** The two multiple methods are trailing by construction — the peer median is computed on the peers' trailing earnings, and a forward peer multiple would need forward peer estimates, which we do not use — so both are struck on FY2025, the first profitable year after the FY2024 loss. The EV/EBITDA method applies the peer median of 11.0x to the restated FY2025 EBITDA of IDR163.2bn [S4], giving Rp465 per share. The P/E method applies 8.5x to FY2025 net profit of IDR35.3bn, or 13.11 per share, giving Rp111, which is -75.9% below the primary.

**The trough is the whole story, in one direction.** The market does not pay the trough multiple. On the model's own forecast the traded price is 11.3x FY2026E EBITDA of IDR381.4bn, 11.5x FY2027E and 11.8x FY2028E — close to the peer median of 11.0x on the forward year. Applying that median forward would therefore return a value near the traded price, not near our DCF: 11.0x times FY2026E EBITDA of IDR381.4bn, less net debt of IDR410.3bn and divided by 2,696.2m shares, gives a per-share value a little below the Rp1,445 price, and the same median on FY2027E and FY2028E EBITDA gives less again because forecast EBITDA is broadly flat. Our cross-check is struck on the trailing trough year, FY2025A restated EBITDA of IDR163.2bn [S4], because the peer median is itself a trailing median and this house does not use forward peer estimates; the forward arithmetic is shown only to make plain that the Rp465 and the DCF's Rp462 land together because the trough year is a fraction of the forward year, which makes the two numbers arithmetic rather than corroboration. We do not present the agreement as a second opinion, and we do not treat the forward-multiple reading as fair value either: it is the price written as a multiple of the same forecast the DCF discounts, and it asks the reader to accept that this company is worth an EBITDA multiple in perpetuity on a margin the DCF fades.

**The divergence we keep.** The P/E result is -75.9% below the primary because a trailing P/E on the first profitable year after a loss is the most distorted number in the set: FY2025 earnings carried the full interest and tax charge of the trough and none of the interim's recovery, and on our FY2026E EPS of 68.34 the same peer multiple would return a value above the DCF. We therefore cut the P/E weight to 10.0% and keep it only so the ladder is visible; the DCF carries 70.0% and the EV/EBITDA cross-check 20.0%. Nothing in the rating rests on the multiple legs — a reader who discards them entirely gets the DCF value of Rp462, and the conclusion is unchanged.

**The peer set.** The median is the industry-wide MATERIALS_OTHER set and it is not a clean benchmark: several constituents are very small, thinly traded converters whose trailing EBITDA is close to nil, and their multiples are many times the median, while the liquid, profitable converters in the table sit at a fraction of it. Excluding the extreme constituents lowers the median and takes the EV/EBITDA cross-check further below the DCF — the bearish direction, not the cautious one. We keep the full set because narrowing it after seeing the answer would be a choice rather than a benchmark; the table below shows every constituent and its trailing multiples, so a reader can re-strike the median.

**Sensitivity.** The two assumptions that carry the valuation are gross margin and the discount rate; a third, working-capital intensity, governs the cash conversion. The grid shows both, and in words: each point of gross margin is worth more than each point of terminal growth, and even the most optimistic corner of the twelve-month grid — two points of margin and four points of growth above the base — is less than half the traded price. The asymmetry matters: the downside from a margin miss is larger than the upside from an equivalent margin beat, because the debt is fixed and the equity absorbs the difference [S0].

**What the price implies.** At Rp1,445 the market capitalisation is IDR3,894.6bn, which is 110.2x FY2025 earnings and 27.2x FY2025 EBITDA on the pack, and 21.1x our FY2026E earnings [S0]. The engine's reverse DCF does not bracket the price, which is the arithmetic version of the last sentence: to justify Rp1,445 on our cash flows the gross margin would have to hold above the 9M2026 record — the highest in the four-year annual-report history [S0][S5] — and fade more slowly than the base assumes, for a decade, at the current leverage; the only other route is that a buyer pays 11.3x forward EBITDA today and sells at an equal or higher multiple at exit, which is the multiple-survival test failing rather than passing. The record of FY2022 to FY2025, with return on equity of 3.4% in the recovery year, does not support that read. The price is paying for the recovery and for its permanence; our value pays for the recovery only, and charges the working-capital build on the way to the equity.

**The quote behind the multiple.** We want to be explicit that the 110.2x trailing multiple above is measured against a thin, post‑unusual‑market‑activity quote, not against a considered market view. The pack's high‑to‑low span over the trailing year is Rp525 to Rp1,955, average daily traded value is only IDR385.1m [S0], and the exchange flagged the stock for counter‑directional movement, suspended it between 16 October and 19 October 2026, and the share then lost -29.9% of that week's level [S8][S9][S10]. We therefore attribute the 110.2x trailing multiple to a post‑UMA speculative print and to the liquidity discount we carry on the target, not to a market that has rationally assessed the recovery as permanent. The fundamental value — and the rating — is unchanged by this; the caveat is that the expected return is a distance between a fair value and an unreliable print, not a twelve‑month forecast.

**Currency and input cost (high likelihood, high impact).** The company buys recovered paper abroad in dollars and sells in rupiah [S4]. A weaker rupiah raises cost of goods directly, and the FY2025 accounts show the mechanism working: revenue grew, margin fell, profit was squeezed [S4]. Our macro regime is balance-of-payments pressure, which tilts the risk toward further depreciation rather than appreciation. This is the risk that matters most, and it is not hedgeable in any meaningful way for a company of this size.

**Commodity price (medium likelihood, high impact).** Recovered-paper prices are set globally and move with Chinese import demand and collection rates. The company has no pricing power over its input and limited ability to pass through quickly, because its customers qualify specifications and shop on price [S4]. A price spike compresses margin within a quarter, and the 9M2026 record margin is the level to defend [S5].

**Leverage and refinancing (low likelihood in the base, high impact in the bear).** Net debt to EBITDA is 3.2 on restated EBITDA at FY2025 and falls to 1.1 in FY2026E on positive cash flow [S0][S4]. Interest cover of about two times in FY2025 widens to about six times on FY2026E operating profit, so the refinancing path is comfortable in the base; the bear case instead carries a cost of debt a point and a half above the house rate, which is the scenario that keeps net debt flat rather than falling [S0]. A covenant event at the margin trough, not in the base, is the most direct route to permanent capital loss, and the FY2024 loss is the precedent [S0].

**Liquidity and float (high likelihood, medium impact).** Free float is 13.7% on the data pack, while the ownership table shows the controller at just over two-thirds and one local individual at a further quarter, leaving the board and a small public block in the remainder [S4][S0]. Average daily traded value is IDR385.1m [S0]. In October 2026 the exchange flagged the stock for counter‑directional movement, suspended trading between 16 October and 19 October, and the share then lost -29.9% of the following week [S8][S9][S10]. In a name this thin, entry and exit move the price, and the quoted price is a poor estimate of realisable value — which is why we apply a liquidity discount of 20.0% to the fundamental value.

**Governance and related parties (low likelihood, medium impact).** The controlling shareholder is a single private company, beneficially owned by two named family members [S4]. We found no material related-party sales or purchases disclosed above the reporting threshold and no pledged controller shares [S4]. The risk is not what is disclosed but what a concentrated controller can do without minority consent — related-party transactions, a capital raise at a discount, or a buyback that transfers cash to selling shareholders at a price above intrinsic value. The buyback approved in June 2026 is small in absolute terms, Rp10.0 billion, but it is being executed at a price far above our value, which is the pattern to watch [S6]. We do not model dilution in the bear: at the traded price a discounted raise would be value-creating on our numbers, so dilution is a tail for the controller rather than a loss channel for the minority [S0].

**Regulatory and trade (low likelihood, medium impact).** Environmental certification requirements and export-market packaging rules are a compliance cost rather than a threat, and the company's certifications are in place [S4]. The bigger tail risk is a change in imported recovered-paper rules or an anti-dumping action affecting the input chain.

**Scenarios.** We run three states of the world, with probabilities of 30.0%, 45.0% and 25.0% for bear, base and bull, worth Rp261, Rp470 and Rp771 per share. The bear case gives back two and a half points of gross margin from the interim record, slows growth by three points and refinances the bank debt a point and a half above the house cost of debt — a plausible replay of the FY2025 squeeze with the currency running the wrong way [S4]. The base case starts at the interim margin and fades it to the through-cycle level, and deleverages on positive cash flow [S5]. The bull case adds two and a half points of margin and three points of growth on cheaper debt, driven by stable currency, lower recovered-paper costs and a mix shift into higher-value sustainable packaging [S4][S5]. The shocks are mirrored across bear and bull, and the values now order bear, base, bull, as they should: with positive cash flow through the explicit period, the growth shock changes working-capital absorption as much as profit, but it no longer inverts the ordering as it did in the initiation build. The direction of the risk is unchanged: the equity is a levered claim on a dollar-cost, rupiah-revenue spread, and the price assumes the favourable side of that spread persists.

**Signposts that would change our view.** A sustained rupiah stronger than the deck path of Rp18,350/USD; gross margin holding above the FY2025 level for several full quarters without volume loss [S5]; net debt to EBITDA falling as the forecast shows; and a decision to stop the buyback and apply the cash to debt [S6]. Conversely, a recovery in recovered-paper prices, a renewed depreciation trend, or a covenant event would move us further down the bear path [S4].

**Ownership and control.** Control sits with PT Golden Arista International, the major and controlling shareholder, which held just over two-thirds of the 2,700,713,744 issued shares at the end of FY2025; its beneficial owners are two named family members, one of them also on the board of commissioners [S4]. The ownership table is the reconciliation: the controller's block, one local individual at a further quarter — listed as a public holder, not as an affiliate or controller — the board's small personal stakes, and the 4,554,100-share treasury position from the buyback [S4]. Against that table the data pack's free float of 13.7% looks high; the unaffiliated public block is about a seventh of the issued shares, and we use the pack figure only for the liquidity discount [S0]. Minority holders cannot block ordinary resolutions, and the practical check on the controller is disclosure and the exchange's listing rules, not the ballot [S4].

**Related parties and pledges.** The annual report discloses affiliation relationships between board members, the controller and the group companies, and it identifies the subsidiaries through which the paper and chemicals operations are run [S4]. We found no material related-party sales or purchases disclosed above the reporting threshold, and no pledge of the controlling block in the annual report or the interim filing [S4] [S5]. That is a clean result on the two channels that most often destroy value on this exchange, and we note it as a positive rather than damn it with faint praise.

**Audit and reporting.** The FY2025 consolidated statements were audited by KAP Hendrik & Rekan, which issued an unqualified opinion, and the same firm signed the prior years [S4]. The nine-month interim statements are unaudited, as is normal on this exchange, and we weight them as the newest actual while the FY2026 accounts settle the fourth quarter [S5]. The data pack's depreciation figure was inconsistent with the notes — the selling-expense line alone discloses IDR4.8bn against the pack's small figure — and the model now restates D&A from the notes at 3.4% of revenue, charging IDR70.8bn in FY2025 [S4].

**Dividends and capital returns.** The dividend has been small and stable: 0.50 per share in the earlier years and 0.50 in FY2025, a yield of 0.50 at the current price [S0]. The board authorised a buyback of up to Rp10.0 billion in June 2026, running to the middle of the following year [S6]. With the forecast now deleveraging on positive cash flow, the buyback does not compete with a funding need, but at Rp1,445 it transfers cash to selling shareholders at several times our estimate of intrinsic value, so we treat it as a signal about management's confidence rather than as valuation support [S0].

**Board.** The board has five commissioners and three directors, with the founding family represented among both [S4]. There is an audit committee and a nomination and remuneration process, and the annual report describes a competency-based selection process for directors [S4]. The structure is typical of a family-controlled Indonesian manufacturer: professional management inside a controlled ownership envelope.

**ESG exposures.** The environmental story is genuine and commercially relevant: the products are made from recycled fibre, the company holds Forest Stewardship Council chain-of-custody certification and ISO quality certification, and it markets the recycled content to export customers facing packaging rules [S4]. The exposures are the mirror image of that: energy intensity in the paper mill, water use and effluent, and the labour intensity of converting. The company reports on these in its sustainability report, employs 885 people directly, and describes health and safety and community programmes in the annual report [S4]. On governance, the concentration of control is the dominant ESG consideration, and it is not mitigated by board independence.

**Dated catalysts.** The FY2026 financial statements, due by the end of the first quarter of 2027, will settle whether the interim margin held through the fourth quarter [S3]. The buyback window closes in the middle of the following year, and the quarterly interim reports in between will show whether the company is funding it from cash or from debt [S6]. Any announcement on the brown-paper machine — an upgrade, a second line or a shutdown — would change the volume and capex assumptions in the model [S4].

**The KPIs we watch.** Gross margin, because it carries most of the valuation and it is the direct transmission channel from the rupiah and recovered-paper prices [S4]; net debt to EBITDA, currently 3.2 on restated EBITDA and falling in our forecast to 0.1, because it is the constraint that would turn a margin miss into a solvency question [S0]; working capital as a share of revenue, at 25.0% in the model, because it is the reason profit and cash diverge [S0]; and the rupiah itself, against the deck path of Rp18,350/USD [S0]. We will also track paper-segment volume against the 234.9 thousand tonnes recorded in FY2025, since volume is the only growth lever the company controls without a price concession [S4].

**How often.** Quarterly, on the interim filings; and immediately on any of the following: a change in the controller's stake, a new debt facility or covenant event, a second buyback authorisation, or a policy change on imported recovered paper [S4]. The next scheduled review is the FY2026 accounts, at which point the audited fourth-quarter margin replaces the interim run-rate in the model [S3].

**What would make us wrong.** A durable margin recovery — the interim accounts already hint at one — combined with a stable rupiah would make the current price less extreme than the multiples suggest, and would move the rating. The error we are guarding against is the opposite: extrapolating a three-month cost tailwind into a decade of returns on capital, which the FY2022-to-FY2025 record does not support [S5][S0].

bear.narrative: Recovered-paper prices normalise and the rupiah weakens past the deck path: gross margin gives back two and a half points from the interim record and growth slows by three points as industrial demand softens, while the bank debt refinances at a rate a point and a half above the house cost of debt [S4]. Interest cover on the FY2025 basis is about two times, so the higher rate is not a covenant event at the debt level we model, but it keeps net debt flat instead of falling, which is the path that matters for holders [S0][S4].

bull.narrative: The interim margin proves structural: lower recovered-paper costs and a mix shift into higher-value sustainable packaging add two and a half points of gross margin and three points of growth, and the bank debt rolls at a rate a point and a half cheaper, so the cash cycle turns and net debt falls faster than in the base [S4][S5].

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is 18%: 9M2026 revenue of 1,882.7bn [S5] plus a fourth quarter of 618.0bn, a little above prior-year Q4 of 562.9bn, gives 2,500.7bn — between a flat prior-year Q4 (2,445.6bn) and the prior-year seasonal weight applied at the 9M growth rate (2,563.7bn). Growth then fades to nominal GDP because the converting plant runs 38.5 of 40.5 kt (95%) [S4] and no material capex commitment is disclosed [S4], so volume cannot compound; price and mix carry the early years.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the 9M2026 actual 21.9% [S5], held for the year because the fourth quarter carries the same recovered-paper and rupiah conditions. It then fades to 16.5% by FY2030E: the interim is above the FY2022 peak of 18.2% [S0], the business has no named moat [S4], and dollar-priced recovered paper is cyclical, so the base does not capitalise a record margin for a decade.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M2026 selling, general and administrative expense is 188.3bn on revenue of 1,882.7bn, 10.0% [S5]; FY2025A was 10.1% [S0]. Held at 10.0% because the cost base is largely fixed distribution and overhead and the company reports efficiency measures offsetting inflation [S4].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the notes: FY2025 depreciation charged to profit or loss was 70.8bn, 3.34% of revenue [S4], not the 7.1bn in the data pack. Held at 3.35% as the brown-paper machine and converting lines are depreciated over 4-20 years [S4]; the pack understates the charge by about 64bn a year.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Sustaining capex set at 3.0% of revenue, close to the restated depreciation charge of 3.34% [S4]. Reported capex of 26.5bn in FY2025 and 43.7bn in FY2024 [S4] ran below D&A in both years and there is no announced expansion project, so the model deliberately holds a maintenance-only regime rather than adding growth capex [S4]. The 0.35pp gap to D&A is the one assumption most likely to flatter free cash flow: if the machine must be replaced at a rate matching depreciation, capex rises by that gap and the value falls. It is disclosed here rather than buried.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set at 25% of revenue, between the FY2025A actual of 26.1% and the FY2023-25 average of 24.1% [S0]. Working capital is the reason profit does not become cash: the FY2025 increase of 151.7bn exceeded operating profit, and the model carries the same intensity as revenue grows.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new facilities are modelled; the forecast free cash flow is positive after the depreciation restatement, so the cycle funds itself and net debt falls from the 9M2026 level of 535.7bn [S0]. A refinancing at a higher rate is in the bear narrative, not the base.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: History pays a flat 0.5 rupiah per share, a payout that has averaged 12% of earnings and 3.8% in FY2025 [S0]. Held at 12%: with leverage at 3.3x restated EBITDA and a buyback of up to Rp10bn running to June 2027 [S6], there is no room for a higher distribution.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No dilution: the buyback is small and discretionary, and no rights issue is announced [S4][S6]. A discounted placement or rights issue is the funding path in the bear case, not the base.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House default 4.0%, below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP growth of 5.3% in the macro deck [S4]. Packaging demand is GDP-sensitive, so a faster perpetual rate would be aggressive; the terminal year also carries 3.0% capex and 25% working-capital intensity, so the cash flow is not inflated.

challenges.challenge: The DCF returns a negative terminal value (-3,102) and negative EV (-1,862), floored at zero and weighted 60% of the target; a negative Gordon TV means terminal FCF is negative, so the DCF is not a valid valuation and the -96% call is an artefact.
challenges.answer: Model rebuilt: every explicit-period FCFF is now positive (156 to 167bn), the terminal value is positive at 2,401bn and the DCF is 461.7 per share with no floor or cap; the old negative TV came from pre-interim assumptions that no longer exist [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The 9M-2026 interim (S5) is described as revenue up 20% and profit several times prior year with visibly higher gross margin, but no fact quantifies it and the base case deliberately excludes it while the report says the rating could move. A base case that knowingly omits the latest actual is stale.
challenges.answer: Added facts F21 revenue 1,882.7bn, F22 gross profit 412.4bn, F23 net profit 172.7bn and prior-year comparatives for 9M2026; FY2026E revenue of 2,500.7bn builds from the interim with a seasonal fourth quarter and no haircut to the 21.9% margin [S5].

challenges.challenge: Gross margin is held at 13.8% (FY2023-25 average) versus FY2025 actual 14.8% and a higher interim, and this 1pp haircut is exactly the -1.0pp calibration gap. The MOST_LIKELY_BASE_CASE card forbids default haircuts without a source.
challenges.answer: Base gross margin is now the 9M2026 actual 21.9%, not the FY2023-25 average, fading to 17.0% by FY2030E with the fade sourced to the FY2022 peak of 18.2% and the absence of a moat; the calibration.ebitda_margin BLOCK is justified in qc_justifications on the interim [S5][S4].

challenges.challenge: The per-share target depends on 2,700,713,744 shares and a 13.7% free float, but no fact F# carries either and S0 price/market cap cannot be verified by grep; the market cap cited (3,894,626,632,080) is asserted without a traceable source.
challenges.answer: Facts added from AR2025 p.68: F16 shares outstanding 2,700,713,744, F17 Golden Arista 1,810,571,784, F18 local individual 686,950,796, F19 treasury 4,554,100. Price 1,445 and market cap 3,894.6bn are the engine market block from the data pack [S0], and the per-share bridge is in section 4 [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: Net debt/EBITDA is 5.3x, interest cover about 2x and FCFF is negative every forecast year, yet the bear scenario is worth more (70) than the base (68) and no covenant, refinancing or equity-raise path is modelled.
challenges.answer: Scenario ordering fixed: bear 251.8, base 430.7, bull 688.4. The bear carries a mirrored cost-of-debt shock of plus 1.5pp against minus 1.5pp in the bull, modelling a refinancing at a higher rate. No covenant breach or dilution is modelled because interest cover is about six times on FY2026E operating profit and the base reaches net cash around FY2031E [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: Revenue growth is held at 14.8% for ten years while the converting plant runs at 95% utilisation (38.5 of 40.5 kt) and capex is only 2.3% of revenue (maintenance); the growth and capex assumptions are mutually inconsistent and the working-capital drag that follows drives the negative FCF.
challenges.answer: Growth cut to fade from 18% in FY2026E to 4.5% by FY2031E, consistent with 95% utilisation of 40.5kt converting capacity; capex is 3.0% of revenue against restated D&A of 3.35%, so no unfunded expansion; the NWC assumption of 25% of revenue is stated in section 3 [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: The report says the EV/EBITDA and P/E cross-checks apply to FY2026E (89.9 EBITDA, 9.1 EPS) and give 203 and 108, but the model uses FY2025A (99.47 EBITDA, 35.34 NP); applying FY2026E would give about 164 and 75, so the text misstates its own method and arithmetic.
challenges.answer: Text corrected to the actual basis: the cross-checks use trailing FY2025A metrics, EV/EBITDA 11.0x on 163.2bn giving 465 and P/E 8.5x on EPS of 13.11 giving 111. The minus 76% P/E divergence is discussed explicitly, with the forward equivalent on FY2026E EPS of 68.3 shown [S0].

challenges.challenge: D&A is 0.36% of revenue in the forecast (7.1 against revenue of 2,432), despite the report noting that the pack understates depreciation (selling-expense depreciation alone is 4.8). The low D&A distorts the EBITDA used in the 20%-weighted EV/EBITDA cross-check.
challenges.answer: D&A restated from the notes: 70.8bn in FY2025 and 68.5bn in FY2024, carried at 3.35% of revenue in the forecast. EBITDA is rebuilt to 163.2bn for FY2025A and 381.4bn for FY2026E, and the EV/EBITDA cross-check runs on the restated figure [S4].

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call justification says to name what the current price implies via a reverse DCF, but the report only asserts that the price discounts a full margin recovery; no reverse DCF or implied-margin calculation is shown, so the -96% call is not evidenced to the house standard.
challenges.answer: The reverse DCF does not bracket the price, so the report states the implied arithmetic: 110x trailing and 21x forward earnings, 27x trailing EV/EBITDA, and a sensitivity grid whose best corner is below half the traded price. The price therefore implies a gross margin above the 9M2026 record held for a decade [S0][S5].

challenges.challenge: The report says a local individual holds about a quarter of shares below the 5% threshold while Golden Arista holds 67.04%, which implies a float nearer 8%, not the 13.7% used; the 20% liquidity discount and ownership narrative are internally inconsistent.
challenges.answer: Float reconciled from the AR2025 ownership table: controller 67.04%, one local individual 25.44%, board about 7.5%, treasury 0.17%, leaving roughly 7% in unaffiliated public hands. The data pack 13.7% is used only for the liquidity discount and the report says it looks high [S4][S0].

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check (20% weight, Rp465) applies the 11.0x peer median to trough FY2025A EBITDA of IDR163.2bn, and s4 presents it as independent corroboration of the DCF ("the DCF and the EBITDA multiple agree within a point, which is the honest centre of this name"). On the model's own forward EBITDA the same multiple gives about Rp1,357/share at FY2026E (381.4), Rp1,299 at FY2027E and Rp1,188-1,190 at FY2029-30E — within 6% of the Rp1,445 price at the near year. The DCF's enterprise value of IDR1,789bn is only 4.4-5.3x the model's steady-state EBITDA of IDR340-404bn, so the two methods do not corroborate each other on any common basis; the "agreement" exists only because 11x is applied to the trough year, which the report itself calls "a disguised forecast". The peer median is also undiscussed: PICO 31.9x, YPAS 18.6x and IPOL 17.1x set it, while the liquid profitable names (IGAR 1.9x, PBID 3.8x, SPMA 7.2x, TRST 7.4x) sit far lower; excluding the three extremes the median is 7.4x and the method returns about Rp247.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the forward arithmetic in words with model placeholders: 11.0x median times FY2026E EBITDA of 381.4bn gives EV of 4,195bn, less net debt of 410.3bn is 3,785bn equity, divided by 2,696.2m shares is about Rp1,404 per share, within 3% of the Rp1,445 price; the same median on FY2027E and FY2028E EBITDA gives about Rp1,346 and Rp1,277, i.e. less again as forecast EBITDA fades [S0]. The basis is stated explicitly as trailing FY2025A because the peer median is itself trailing and this house does not use forward peer estimates [S0][S4]. The peer set paragraph explains the 11.0x median is set by PICO, YPAS and IPOL, that excluding the extremes lowers it, and that the full set is kept to avoid choosing a benchmark after seeing the answer. The "agree within a point" and "honest centre" language is removed from both section 4 and the Investment summary.

challenges.challenge: The extreme_call qc_justification still reads "multiples (EV/EBITDA 11.0x median, P/E 8.5x median) and DCF (positive TV) converge ~461". The P/E method returns Rp111, -75.9% below the DCF, which s4 itself reports; there is no three-way convergence. The same justification calls Rp353 the "fundamental value" when Rp353 is the post-20%-liquidity-discount target and the pre-discount value is Rp462 (base) or Rp441 (probability-weighted).
challenges.answer: qc_justifications.extreme_call rewritten: it no longer claims three-way convergence. It names the two drivers of the -73% call, the gross-margin fade from the 9M2026 actual 21.9% to 16.5% by FY2030E [S5][S4] and the 20% liquidity discount on a float of roughly a seventh of the shares [S4], states that the EV/EBITDA cross-check is the 11.0x median on trough FY2025A EBITDA and the P/E 111 is the trough-basis outlier at -76% rather than a third estimate, and describes 386 as the post-discount target (pre-discount 482 weighted, 470 base), consistent with section 4. The engine was re-run and the QC gate now reads the corrected justification.

challenges.challenge: Open note Q9: fund record revenue_growth basis still says a fourth quarter at the prior-year seasonal weight gives about 2,500bn, while the prior-year seasonal weight gives 2,563.7bn and the report now says "a little above the prior-year seasonal quarter" (FY2026E Q4 of 618.0bn against prior-year Q4 of 562.9bn). The file and the report disagree.
challenges.answer: The fund record revenue_growth basis now states the fourth-quarter figure actually used: FY2026E Q4 of 618.0bn against prior-year Q4 of 562.9bn, giving FY2026E revenue of 2,500.7bn, and it shows that this sits between a flat prior-year Q4 (2,445.6bn) and the prior-year seasonal weight applied at the 9M growth rate (2,563.7bn) [S5][S0]. The file now matches the report FY2026E build.

challenges.challenge: Open note Q10: F38 w52_high_uma_date duplicates F32 price_uma_15oct2026 (both 1,955) and S10 describes 1,955 as the close of the week before the UMA, not the 15 October close; the fact labels are duplicated and misdated.
challenges.answer: F38 is dropped. F32 is relabelled and rekeyed to price_pre_uma_week_close with the label "ALDO close of the week before the 19-23 Oct 2026 selloff (pre-UMA reference price)", period 20261016, value 1,955 and the verbatim S10 quote that describes 1,955 as the prior-week close against the 23 October close of 1,370 [S10]. cov_report check was re-run and returns PASS.

missing_bull_case.note: The 9M-2026 interim (S5) shows revenue up about 20% and profit several times prior year, but no facts quantify it and the bull scenario only adds 1.5pp margin; the demonstrated interim upside is excluded from base and bull. Understates the bull case.

missing_bear_case.note: Debt spiral understated: net debt/EBITDA 5.3x, FCFF negative every forecast year, interest cover about 2x. No covenant, refinancing or equity-raise scenario; buyback competes with deleveraging. Bear value (70) is above base, so downside is not actually modelled.

assumption_realism.note: Revenue growth held at 14.8% for a decade while the converting plant runs 38.5 of 40.5 kt (95% utilisation) and capex is maintenance-only at 2.3%; growth and capex are mutually inconsistent. Gross margin 13.8% sits below FY2025 actual 14.8% with no sourced reason.

evidence_and_citations.note: Share count (2,700,713,744) and free float 13.7% are load-bearing for a -96% call but no fact F# carries them; S0 price cannot be grepped. The report also says the EV/EBITDA and P/E cross-checks use FY2026E metrics when the model uses FY2025A (99.47 EBITDA, 35.34 NP).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF terminal value is -3,102 and PV of TV -1,174, giving EV -1,862 and equity -2,407; the engine floors this at zero and it is then weighted 60%. A negative Gordon TV is a broken model, not a valuation. The claim that TV carries 63% of total describes 63% of a negative number.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose repeatedly admits the interim shows a materially higher earnings base and that the rating could move, yet publishes SELL -96%; the conclusion is driven by one degenerate DCF input. Reverse-DCF demanded by the extreme_call flag is asserted, not computed.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No konglo or sector-deck variables (benchmark, realisation basis, royalty) apply to this converter; the macro deck (USD/IDR 18,350 FY2027E) is used consistently.

conservatism_audit.note: Stack of below-actual/unsourced assumptions: gross margin 13.8% vs 14.8% actual and higher interim; 14.8% growth with maintenance capex; D&A held at 0.36% of revenue despite the report noting that the pack understates depreciation; scenario shocks are asymmetric and inverted (bear 70 above bull 67).

calibration.note: The QC calibration gate shows model FY+1 EBITDA margin 3.69% vs FY2025A actual 4.69% (-1.0pp), which is the gross-margin haircut flowing through. The drift is not answered in qc_justifications; only scenario.order and extreme_call are.

signoff.notes: Round 2. Approved on substance. The four round-1 MATERIAL challenges are fixed. L1: section 4 now shows the forward EV/EBITDA arithmetic (11.0x on FY2026E EBITDA of 381.4bn, less FY2026E net debt of 410.3bn, over 2,696.2m shares, a little below the 1,445 price) beside the 465, states and sources the trailing-trough basis, justifies the full peer set, and removes the independent-corroboration language from section 4 and the summary. L2: the extreme_call justification no longer claims three-way convergence, names the DCF 462 and EV/EBITDA 465 as the pairing and the trough-basis P/E 111 as the -76% outlier, and restates the post-discount target as 386 (pre-discount 482 weighted, 470 base). L3: the revenue_growth basis states the FY2026E Q4 of 618.0bn against 562.9bn, the 2,500.7bn total and the 2,445.6-2,563.7bn bracket, matching the report. L4: F38 is dropped and F32 is rekeyed and relabelled as the pre-UMA week close of 1,955 with the S10 quote. cov_report check passes on facts and lint; QC round 2 passes with no BLOCK. Base case is anchored, not haircut: FY2026E gross margin 21.9% equals the 9M2026 actual, opex 10.0% equals the 9M actual, D&A 3.35% is restated from the notes, and FY2026E revenue of 2,500.7bn sits between a flat prior-year Q4 and the seasonal weight. Scenario shocks are mirrored (revenue +/-3pp, gross margin +/-2.5pp, cost of debt +/-1.5pp), probabilities are base 45%, bear 30%, bull 25%, and the ordering is bear 261 < base 470 < bull 771.
